_mod_info: Dialogue lines spoken by VCs during fundraising meetings. Each category is used at a specific point in the pitch flow. Lines are picked randomly, filtered by tier/economy/round when those fields are present.

openings.text: We've been watching your space. Walk us through the numbers.
Our partners were split on taking this meeting. Convince us.
We read the deck. Now tell us what the deck doesn't say.
I've got 30 minutes. Make me believe.
Interesting space. The question is whether you can own it.
So. You're burning how much per quarter?
A friend of a friend vouched for you. That bought you this meeting.
We took a similar meeting last week. They didn't get a second one.
I'll be honest — I almost passed on this. Glad I didn't cancel.
Let's skip the vision slide. What's actually working?
We like the sector. The real question is why you and why now.
My partner says your metrics remind her of a company we backed in '19.
We've funded six companies in this space. Tell us what you'd do differently.
First — before we get into anything — who's your customer and what's the pain?
I read the blog post your CTO published last month. Thoughtful stuff. Let's talk.
Alright, the floor is yours. No slides, just talk to us.
We don't usually take meetings this early. Your growth curve got our attention.
Our thesis is about markets, not products. Tell us about the market.
Quick ground rules: we're going to challenge every number. Don't take it personally.
We keep things informal. Grab a coffee and tell us the story.
We're an early believer fund. Proof points matter less than founder conviction.

questions.text: What does your retention look like after 90 days?
Walk me through unit economics. What's your CAC to LTV?
What happens when a bigger player copies your main feature?
Tell me about a decision you almost got wrong.
If we gave you double the money, what would you do differently?
What's the one metric that keeps you up at night?
How do you think about pricing power as you scale?
Where does the next 10x in users come from?
Tell me about your team. Who's employee number one?
What's your honest assessment of your biggest competitor right now?
Walk me through your worst quarter. What did you learn?
How are you thinking about international expansion?
If the market turns tomorrow, how many quarters can you survive?
What would make you walk away from this company?
What part of the product are you most proud of shipping?

reactions_positive: Those numbers are better than I expected. Let's keep talking.
OK — now you have my attention.
That's a growth rate we don't see often at this stage.
Solid. That's the kind of trajectory that compounds.
Our portfolio company in this space would kill for those metrics.
I just texted my partner. She's going to want to hear this too.
This is cleaner than most Series A decks I see. And you're earlier.
Good margins. Good retention. You're doing something right.
reactions_neutral: Interesting. Not where I expected it to be, but interesting.
The numbers tell a mixed story. Walk me through the trend lines.
There's signal here, but I'm not sure it's strong enough yet.
We've seen similar traction. The question is whether it holds.
Decent foundation. I'd want to see another quarter before committing.
Some of these numbers land, some don't. Let's unpack that.
It's early. Hard to call at this stage.
You're in the zone where this could break either way.
reactions_negative: I'll be candid — these numbers are below our threshold.
The burn concerns me. You're spending faster than you're learning.
I see the vision, but the metrics don't support it yet.
You're going to have a hard time raising at this valuation with these numbers.
We've passed on stronger traction in this space. I'll be honest with you.
This feels too early for us. Come back with stronger proof points.
I want to be excited, but the churn is telling me something.
Your team is promising. The numbers aren't there yet.
offer_lines: We'd like to move forward. Here's what we're thinking.
We want in. Let me lay out the terms.
Good meeting. We're prepared to make an offer today.
My partners and I talked it over. We'd like to be part of this.
Let's cut to it — we want to invest. Here are the terms.
We believe in what you're building. This is what we can do.
I called my partners on the way back. We have a term sheet ready.
Don't sign anything else yet. We want to lead this round.

elite: Not enough traction for our thesis right now.
We loved the pitch, but we need to see stronger unit economics.
Impressive team, but the market fit isn't there yet for us.
We have a portfolio conflict in this space. Can't move forward.
The opportunity size doesn't match our fund model. Come back when you're bigger.
We're going to pass. But I'd take your next meeting with our growth fund.
Candidly, we think the market timing is off. Check back in two quarters.
Strong founder. But we need to see revenue, not projections.
Our investment committee couldn't get to consensus. That's a no for now.
top: We're going to pass for now — come back when you hit $1M ARR.
The space is interesting but we need more proof points.
Good foundation, but we'd want to see faster growth before committing.
We like you as a founder. The business needs more seasoning.
Too early for our stage. Have you talked to seed funds?
We just closed a deal in adjacent territory. Conflict of interest.
The competitive landscape gives us pause. Too many well-funded players.
There's something here, but we can't get comfortable on the valuation.
mid: We'll keep in touch. Not the right time for us.
Interesting business, but not quite the fit we're looking for this fund.
We appreciate the meeting. Let's reconnect next quarter.
We're overallocated in this sector right now. Bad timing.
Not a no forever — just a no right now. Keep building.
We need to see more traction before we can pull the trigger.
Good pitch. We're going to marinate on it. Follow up in 90 days.
We like what you're doing but our partners want to see a trend, not a moment.
emerging: This is a bit beyond our check size at this stage. We wish you well.
We're a smaller fund. Can't stretch to this round size.
We love the mission, but our portfolio is full this quarter.
Honestly, you should be talking to bigger firms. You've outgrown us.
We'd have said yes six months ago. Our fund is mostly deployed now.
Not the right fit for our thesis, but I'm going to make an intro for you.
We admire the hustle. The economics just aren't there for our model yet.

acceptance_celebrations: Welcome to the portfolio. Now the real work begins.
Deal closed. Let's go build something.
You just leveled up. Don't let the money make you lazy.
Congrats. I'll introduce you to three companies in our network this week.
Money's wiring now. Spend it wisely — we'll be watching.
Great outcome. Now hit those milestones or our next meeting will be different.
We backed you because we believe. Prove us right.
The hard part wasn't raising. The hard part starts now.
